Subject: pgvector + S3 listing: marketplace onboarding, schema mapping, and legal checklist

Hi Elena / pgvector team —

Quick note from Redwood on the joint listing we discussed at partner week. We want to get the technical and commercial checklist aligned so we can submit to CloudVendor Marketplace next quarter. High-level asks: 

- Confirmation of minimal schema requirements for pgvector-compatible indexes when layered over S3 (index mapping, chunking semantics, metadata fields we should expose).
- Any special runtime or plugin your team expects when calling pgvector with S3-backed vectors (latency/consistency caveats).
- A short list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2, encryption at rest, data residency statements) that the marketplace requires.
- Marketplace submission: contact for the marketplace team and a pointer to the submission form + contract flow (DocuSign or e-sign).

I attached a draft integration_spec_v1.pdf that captures the proposed mapping Redwood would surface in the console (fields, retention knobs, rehydration path). Can you review and flag any blockers?

Goal: submit by July 6th so listing can be live for August enablement. If useful, let's lock a 30-min technical sync — proposed windows Thursday or Friday (Ben/Laura/Karthik available).

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: pgvector + S3 listing: marketplace onboarding, schema mapping, and legal checklist

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the spec — this is a great starting point. High-level answers inline: 

- Schema: we recommend a canonical set of metadata fields: id, embedding_version, chunk_id, source_uri (S3 path), text_excerpt, created_at, tenant_id (if multi-tenant). pgvector consumers expect stable id + embedding_version so you can rotate vectors without breaking lookups. Also include a namespace tag for per-customer isolation; we saw lots of issues when vendors co-mingled indexes.

- Runtime caveats: S3-backed stores typically add ~5–25ms per fetch for cold shards; make sure your cache prewarm policy and KV cache TTLs are explicit in the docs. If Redwood intends to do prefix/KV caching (recommended) expose an endpoint to invalidate per-tenant keys. Quantization/IPP artifacts are fine — just document model dimension and dtype.

- Compliance: Pinecone requires a SOC2 attestation (we can share a copy), encryption at rest + in transit statements, and export controls form for marketplace. Marketplace may ask for a short privacy/dataflow diagram. We can attach our SOC2 roster — attaching pinecone_onboard_guide.pdf which contains the marketplace checklist we used last quarter.

- Marketplace flow: CloudVendor accepts partner submissions via an online form; final contract is DocuSign. The contact there is cloudmarketplace@vendor.com and the submission URL is in the attached guide (see section 2). They typically return a contract template in 3–5 business days.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Technical sync Thursday 2028-06-27 at 10:00 PT — Elena + Pinecone engineer + Ben/Laura/Karthik + pgvector rep.
2) Pinecone will drop SOC2 excerpt and the onboarding guide (attached).
3) Redwood to update integration_spec_v1.pdf with the namespace and id conventions; we can then prepare the marketplace submission draft.

If you want, Pinecone can introduce the pgvector team to the CloudVendor PM directly during the sync.

Best,
Elena

--

Strategic Partnerships | Pinecone
elena@pinecone.io

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Elena Martins <elena@pinecone.io>, pgvector-team@pgvector.org
Date: 2028-06-26 08:45 -07:00
Subject: Re: pgvector + S3 listing: marketplace onboarding, schema mapping, and legal checklist

Ben — quick internal readout before the sync. A few legal/commercial points we need to address so sales and marketplace folks don't get blocked: 

- Contract: marketplace typically wants a single-line item for "Redwood Inference — PGVector Connector" with clear support SLAs. Legal will want to negotiate liability/indemnity clauses if we're co-selling. I'll loop Revenue Ops for pricing SKU guidance.

- Data residency & residency claims: confirm whether pgvector will allow a "regional only" option for EU customers; marketplace may require that as a listing attribute. If pgvector can't guarantee, we need to mark the listing as "global" and call out residency caveats.

- Compliance artifacts: ask Pinecone for the SOC2 snapshot + encryption blurb (Elena already attached helpful material). Redwood will supply the privacy/dataflow diagram (I can draft a short one for the submission).

- Billing model: figure out whether we list "connector" as free + usage billed via Redwood, or as a paid add-on in CloudVendor catalog. This affects the doc flow for the submission. Karthik, can your commercialization playbook weigh in (per-seat vs per-token vs flat connector fee)?

I will prep a redlined marketplace contract template and the DocuSign link so we can move quickly once technical sign-off is done. Also prepared to write the short listing blurb (200 words) once we agree on features and residency.

Action items for the sync: Laura to cover legal bullets and listing wording; Ben to present integration_spec_v1; Karthik to present pricing options.

Thanks — see you on the 27th.

Laura
